name: TX-33
label: Safe D

key_factors: Colin Allred's large fundraising advantage and name recognition
Open seat after Crockett's retirement, but seat stays with the incumbent party
model.rationale: TX-33's D+18 partisan lean makes this a heavily Democratic open seat, and Colin Allred's $7.4 million in fundraising dwarfs an underfunded Republican opponent. Markets price Democrats around 96%, consistent with a Safe D rating.
model.watch: Any late surge in Republican outside spending or a polling surprise showing a single-digit race would warrant a downgrade.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Jasmine Crockett (D) is not on the ballot.

overview: Jasmine Crockett's retirement leaves TX-33 an open seat, but the district's D+18 partisan lean keeps it firmly in Democratic hands. Former Rep. Colin Allred, the Democratic nominee, brings high name recognition from his 2024 Senate run and has raised over $7.4 million, while Republican Patrick Gillespie reports minimal fundraising. Prediction markets price a Democratic win near 96%, and no expert raters flag the race as competitive. The forecast expects a comfortable Democratic margin in the low twenties, with modest uncertainty given the absence of public polling in this safely blue Dallas-area district.
